stories.primary_headline: Karnataka High Court quashes POCSO charges against father, family members

primary_source.headline: Karnataka High Court quashes POCSO charges against father, family members
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has quashed proceedings against a man, his parents and sister under the provisions of the POCSO Act over allegations of sexual harassment on his minor child. “The innocence of childhood cannot be made the currency with which matrimonial scores are settled. Equally, the protection of a child cannot be sacrificed at the altar of a parent's claim of false implication,” Justice M Nagaprasanna said while allowing the petition filed by the father of the child and his family members.The estranged couple, residing in Bengaluru, had been involved in pleas over the custody and companionship of their minor daughter. The husband was awarded visitation rights as per the orders of the family court as well as the high court. Mangaluru court sentences two men to 20 years rigorous imprisonment in separate POCSO casesOn May 16 and May 17, 2026, the child was with the father but after returning, the mother alleged that the daughter complained of discomfort around her private parts. An FIR was registered under sections 8 and 10 of the POCSO Act against the father and other members of his family. Pursuant to the complaint, the mother approached the high court seeking cancellation/modification of the visitation rights granted to the father, citing the registration of the FIR. Challenging the FIR, the petitioners contended the allegation was made of sexual harassment of the minor child by the father and his family members.After perusing the affidavits placed by the doctors of the hospital where the child was subjected to medical examination, Justice Nagaprasanna noted that the complaints of discomfort were described as non-specific clinical findings. “Had the doctors expressed an opinion that the findings were attributable to sexual assault, the matter would have presented an altogether different complexion. That is not what the affidavits placed before this Court disclose,” the court said.The court further said that a contest for the custody and companionship of a minor daughter has resulted in drawing the child into the vortex of criminal litigation. “The child, who ought to have been the beneficiary of the affection of both parents, is now at the centre of their adversarial battle. The discord between the parents appears to have travelled far beyond the boundaries of their matrimonial relationship and threatens to cast its shadow upon the innocence, emotional security and well-being of the child,” Justice Nagaprasanna said.The court further said, “The criminal law cannot be reduced to a means of achieving indirectly what a litigant seeks to secure directly in proceedings concerning custody and visitation. The process of law is meant to advance justice, not to become the punishment itself.”

brief_bullets: The Karnataka High Court has quashed POCSO charges against a father and his family members, ruling that the allegations were weaponized during a contentious child custody battle. Justice M. Nagaprasanna determined that medical evidence failed to substantiate claims of sexual assault, describing the findings as non-specific and noting the absence of clinical proof. The court emphasized that the child was unfairly drawn into an adversarial parental dispute, warning that criminal litigation should not be used to settle matrimonial scores or manipulate visitation rights. By dismissing the FIR, the judiciary underscored that the integrity of child protection laws must be preserved against misuse, ensuring that legal processes serve justice rather than becoming tools for personal retaliation in domestic conflicts.
why_it_matters_bullets: This ruling sets a critical precedent against the weaponization of child protection laws in high-stakes matrimonial custody disputes.

stories.primary_headline: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw urges social media platforms to take greater responsibility for online harms

primary_source.headline: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw urges social media platforms to take greater responsibility for online harms
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Social media platforms must assume greater responsibility for the content they host, take necessary steps to ensure child safety, ensure algorithmic transparency, and provide citizens with an effective mechanism to address grievances, Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday.Speaking on the evolving nature of the internet and social media landscape, Vaishnaw asserted that platforms can no longer remain passive. They must proactively protect society from serious online harms, including “digital arrest” scams, he said. Kolkata teen blindfolded, set ablaze; police arrest 3, assault allegedly filmed for social media reel “Today, social media platforms must take the responsibility for child safety, for women’s safety, for digital arrest, for the harms which come to the citizens… social media platforms must take proactive steps. Unlike the past, they must take proactive steps to make sure that our society is safe,” said Vaishnaw, who also holds the Information and Broadcasting portfolio.The minister stressed the need to give ordinary citizens a stronger voice on these platforms. Currently, he noted, when content causes serious harm, the only options available are approaching the courts or the police. He called for a robust and effective grievance redressal system that allows people to seek remedies directly.“If something is there on the social media platforms which causes serious harm to the citizens, the citizens have only the recourse to go to the courts or go to the police. There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which the citizens get voice to address their grievances,” Vaishnaw said.

In jailing Joshua Wong, China is telling the world they'd crush every hope for democracy on its soil | Nathan Law

brief_bullets: Prominent Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to an additional ten years in prison under the territory's national security law, effectively extending his incarceration until 2036. Convicted of colluding with foreign forces, Wong was identified by the court as a mastermind behind international advocacy efforts, including lobbying for sanctions against Chinese and Hong Kong officials. This ruling, which cites his previous leadership in the youth-led party Demosistō and his extensive history of political activism, marks the second time Wong has been convicted under the sweeping security legislation. The decision underscores the intensifying crackdown on dissent in Hong Kong, signaling a permanent shift in the region's political landscape and the systematic dismantling of the pro-democracy movement.
why_it_matters_bullets: The extended sentencing signals a permanent end to organized political opposition and deepens the erosion of Hong Kong's autonomy.

sources.headline: Nora Fatehi tells Delhi court Sukesh Chandrasekhar’s wife Leena introduced them
'In India On Work Visa': Nora Fatehi Tells Court In Sukesh Chandrasekhar Case

brief_bullets: Bollywood actor Nora Fatehi testified before a Delhi court, clarifying that her initial introduction to alleged conman Sukesh Chandrasekhar was facilitated by his wife, Leena Paulose. During the proceedings, Fatehi detailed her interactions with the couple, specifically recounting a trip to Chennai where she met Paulose. This testimony serves as a critical development in the ongoing money laundering investigation involving Chandrasekhar, who is accused of orchestrating a massive extortion scheme. By distancing herself from direct involvement with the primary accused and highlighting Paulose’s role as the intermediary, Fatehi’s statement provides investigators with essential context regarding the social network utilized by the suspects to gain access to high-profile figures within the entertainment industry.
why_it_matters_bullets: This testimony complicates the legal defense for the accused and highlights the vulnerability of celebrities to sophisticated financial exploitation.

Japan’s former soccer chief aims to run against Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency - CNN

brief_bullets: Japanese media reports indicate that FIFA Council member and former Japanese soccer chief Kohzo Tashima intends to challenge incumbent Gianni Infantino for the presidency of world football's governing body. This unfolding electoral contest introduces a rare high-profile institutional challenge against Infantino, whose tenure has faced intense global scrutiny over governance, commercial expansions, and tournament scheduling. Tashima's potential candidacy signals growing internal friction among regional federations regarding FIFA's centralized leadership and strategic trajectory ahead of the upcoming presidential vote.
why_it_matters_bullets: This challenge threatens Infantino's consolidation of power, potentially catalyzing broader resistance within global football governance.
